processes.description: Credit and desk leads tell the real-time traders when a counterparty is cut off or cleared to trade again, in short all-desk notices, and the risk side asks for or confirms credit reserves on named transactions. A reserve request is forwarded with the deal details below it, and the reply states how origination was split between the trader and the credit reserve, with any balance taken from the trader's origination that night.
steps: Credit decides a counterparty is restricted or cleared, or a transaction needs a reserve.
The desk lead sends a notice to the real-time group naming the counterparty and whether trading is allowed.
Risk forwards the transaction details and asks for a credit reserve to be taken.
The reserve and origination split is booked and confirmed back to the trader.
Any shortfall in the split is corrected by moving origination from the trader's book.

stalls.summary: A reserve allocation had to be redone after the original split, with extra origination pulled from the trader the same night.

automation.approach: Keep a single counterparty credit status list that the deal-entry system checks before a trade is booked, and have a reserve request form that captures the deal numbers and the split between trader origination and credit reserve, so the booking and confirmation come from one record instead of free-text email.
automation.rationale: The rounds are short notices and reserve requests; a standard notice and reserve-request message with fixed fields (counterparty, status, effective time, deal numbers, reserve amount, split) would remove ambiguity and the rework seen when a split is corrected afterwards.

work_estimate.rationale: A round is either a status notice, which needs only a quick check of the credit decision and updating the desk's counterparty list, or a reserve request, which needs the deal looked up, the reserve calculated and booked and the split confirmed. Both are small, bounded tasks, so the mid sits near ten minutes, with the high end covering a reserve that must be rebooked.

processes.description: Marketing and facility planning work up proposed pipeline interconnects and expansions. A request for an interconnect arrives and is handed to a marketing contact with a planning counterpart; facility planning engineers then produce cost estimates, listing the work needed to make an interconnect bi-directional, pressure ranges and spreadsheets of build costs, sometimes split out for interest, overheads and AFUDC at marketing's request. Maps and facility data are gathered from field staff, and meetings are set to discuss pressure scenarios and facility modifications with the customer.
steps: A customer or marketing raises a proposed interconnect or expansion project.
A marketing contact and a facility planning counterpart are named for the request.
Planning gathers facility information and maps from field offices.
Engineers prepare a cost estimate and the list of work required, with pressure ranges.
The estimate spreadsheet is reworked to marketing's requested layout and sent on.
Marketing schedules a meeting with the customer to review pressures, modifications and costs.

stalls.summary: Cost estimates wait on facility information from field staff before they can be finished.
Getting a map that shows the power plant location took longer than expected.
Who is the marketing contact for a new interconnect is settled by email each time, with planning asking who its counterpart will be.

automation.approach: Use a standard interconnect request intake that names the marketing and planning owners at the start, and a cost estimate spreadsheet layout that already breaks out interest, overheads and AFUDC by line item along with pressure ranges, so estimates arrive in the form marketing needs without a second pass.
automation.rationale: The repeated effort is assembling cost estimates and reformatting them for marketing; a fixed estimate layout and intake form addresses both the reformatting request and the owner confusion, while the engineering judgement stays with planning.

work_estimate.rationale: Most rounds carry an engineering cost estimate: listing the work to make an interconnect bi-directional, pricing it, adding pressure ranges and building the spreadsheet, plus gathering maps and field facility data. Some rounds are only scheduling a meeting or assigning a contact, which keeps the low end small; a full level A estimate pushes the high end. Only the spreadsheet assembly and formatting are readily automated.

processes.description: The real-time desk lead sends the shift traders a steady stream of instructions and position updates: open longs and shorts by hub and hour, purchases and sales to enter in Enpower under named books, deal numbers to use for transmission, checkout calls with marketers and utilities each night, and the monthly shift schedule. Traders keep preschedule and EPE schedule sheets, submit schedules and tags to the CISO, and correct mistakes found afterwards, such as wrong import IDs, duplicate schedules, wrong lending amounts or schedules misentered by the CISO.
steps: The desk lead or preschedulers report the day's positions and deals by hub and hour.
Shift traders enter purchases and sales in Enpower under the right books and deal numbers.
Schedules and tags are submitted to the CISO and counterparties, with hourly calls where required.
Traders check out with major marketers and utilities each night.
Errors in the schedule sheets, tags or CISO entries are found and corrected.
Shift coverage and rule changes are circulated to the group.

stalls.summary: Schedule sheets repeatedly carry errors that have to be reworked: duplicate schedules, wrong lending positions and missing schedules in the EPE sheet.
Wrong import IDs and schedules misentered at the CISO force corrections after submission.
Systems fail during the shift: the CISO cannot read submitted bids, trading screens stop working and Enpower is taken down for maintenance.
When deals are not recorded during a shift, traders on that shift have to reconstruct the sheet afterwards.
A requested task was put off to another day for lack of time.

contradictions.summary: The EPE schedule sheets disagree with the actual lending deals: the sheet showed a lending position the desk had to correct, and later the lending in the EPE schedules was recorded at a different volume from the deal with PSCO.
A trader's spreadsheet showed a dispatch figure that the desk lead questioned against what was actually scheduled.

automation.approach: Generate the preschedule and EPE schedule sheets from the deals booked in Enpower, with checks that flag duplicate schedules, lending volumes that differ from the deal, and import IDs or tags that do not match the CISO submission. A nightly checkout report listing positions by counterparty and hour would replace manual reconciliation, and a written shift procedure would hold the standing rules now repeated by email.
automation.rationale: Much of the email restates standing rules (hourly calls, deal numbers for transmission, nightly checkout, where to book real-time purchases) and corrects sheet errors. A desk procedure gives every shift the same rules, and the generated sheets with checks attack the rework that recurs most.

work_estimate.rationale: A round usually means entering or adjusting deals in Enpower, updating the preschedule or EPE sheet, and checking positions or tags against the CISO and counterparties; correction rounds add finding and fixing a wrong import ID, lending volume or duplicate schedule, and occasionally reconstructing a shift's sheet. Simple position notices take little; reconstruction drives the high end. Sheet building and mismatch checks are the automatable part.
